items.title: Ray Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, AZ, April 16, 2000
items.q: You guys seem to have no lack of sense of humor in the Oscar Peterson Trio. Is that a fair statement?

ctx.x: Oh yeah. Because you’ve got to remember the arrangement part of jazz is only in certain spots. There’s a lot of freedom for guys to blow, everybody has got a lot of free space there. And I mean if you hear somebody play the same tune five nights in a row, the blowing’s going to be different. The parts are the same, but the blowing’s different. And if you get a jam session like one of these jam sessions here, if you’ve got the same group to play together for three weeks, five or six nights a week, they would start…
Yeah. You guys seem to have no lack of sense of humor in the Oscar Peterson Trio. Is that a fair statement?
Well when we were young we did a lot of crazy things. I think everybody does. Nobody has a corner on that. If we all go back to when we were young, we carried on.

items.title: Oscar Peterson interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: So while we were teaching, on off periods, I would call the group together in the school and we’d get in a room somewhere, and we’d put together arrangements on the album.

ctx.x: An album, yeah, yeah. And I must say, your “West Side Story” touches, I mean it’s poignant when it needs to be poignant, it says so much, feeling and glory and happiness, and all the facets. You show it at the piano, and with your group, and with the people you work with.
Well I have to tell you the story on “West Side Story,” on that album. We had this school, the jazz school in Toronto, called The Advanced School for Contemporary Music, and it

was Ray Brown, Ed Thigpen and myself. And we were teaching there. And I got a call from Verve records and they said, “we would like you to do something on ‘West Side Story.’” And I said, oh, boy, I’d heard some of the score and that’s not easy, you know. So they said, “could you put something together and we’d like to do it soon, because the show is hot, and we’d like to get it out.” You know like record companies, it’s like do it yesterday. So while we were teaching, on off periods, I would call the group…
